Chapter scope (〜じ〜ふん, 〜から〜まで, verb ます／ません／ました／ませんでした, ね, noun です／でした) is a published textbook sequence reference; all wording here is original.
JLPT band is a placement heuristic, not a score claim.

provenance.castingNote: Grammar picks the person: chapter 4 is times and weekly plans, so it belongs to Angel (who already has everyone's week on a spreadsheet) and Jodi (calm, always early), with Rie teaching. The first-kanji strand — the numbers on the clock and 日 — is framed as Shin's, the classmate who reads kanji as little pictures.

runtimeReachability.honestResult: Package data is authored and source-traced; runtime reachability still requires forbidden adapter, hash, catalog, and media registration edits.

delivery.beat: Jenny and Tom compare dated schedule cards and complete the source past-tense noun problems in order.

steps.evidence: Follow an ordinary day, then hear classmates arrange a meeting time and day.

steps.form: N じに Vます。N じから N じまで Vます。N ようびでした。
steps.meaning: Place actions in a daily schedule and identify a past day.
steps.contrast: でした says a past state; ます／ません／ました／ませんでした change the action time or polarity.
steps.workedExample: げつようびは 9じから 5じまで はたらきました。

steps.activity: Read the study-meet notice and match the day, time, and verb form to its meaning.

progressiveHints: Put から after the start.
Add the end time plus まで before the verb.

feedback.error: If から and まで are reversed or one is missing, the time span is not recoverable.
feedback.retry: Trace the time line from start to finish and enter the full span.

progressiveHints: Choose a day and two times.
Add one から〜まで span and one bedtime sentence.

feedback.error: If the question back has no か or a time has no じ, the partner cannot answer clearly.
feedback.retry: Use the day-and-time note, then ask one complete question.

progressiveHints: List your three actions in English first.
Give each action a Japanese clock time.
Use the taught polite ending for the intended time.

feedback.error: If the long vowel in a weekday is missing or the verb form contradicts the schedule, the meaning changes.
feedback.retry: Check the time word and verb ending, then rewrite the one mismatch.

learningObjectives: Tell the time with 〜じ〜ふん and ask いま なんじですか.
Say what you do each day with your first verbs — おきます, ねます, はたらきます — in the do / don't / did / didn't forms.
Give a span of time with 〜から〜まで (くじから ごじまで).
Say what day it is, and what day it was, with です／でした, and check gently with ね.
Read and hand-write your first kanji on the clock: 一・二・三・日.

explanation.recap: Last week you were shopping — これを ください, asking いくらですか, and reading prices out loud. Keep those numbers warm: tonight the very same いち・に・さん become the clock and the days of the week.
explanation.intro: Everything tonight runs on time. You'll say what time it is (〜じ〜ふん), talk about your day with your first real verbs (おきます, ねます, はたらきます, and their did / didn't forms), stretch a span from one time to another with 〜から〜まで, and check the day gently with ね. By the end you can tell a friend, in Japanese, exactly how your week goes.

grammarPoints.pattern: 〜じ〜ふん ／ いま なんじですか
grammarPoints.nameJa: いま なんじですか
grammarPoints.meaning: telling and asking the time — o'clock (じ) and minutes (ふん／ぷん)
grammarPoints.explanation: A time is a number + じ for the hour and a number + ふん／ぷん for the minutes: くじ = 9 o'clock, くじ じゅっぷん = 9:10. Ask the time with いま なんじですか ('what time is it now?'). A few readings bend: 4 o'clock is よじ (never よんじ), 7 is しちじ, 9 is くじ. The minute word switches between ふん and ぷん — いっぷん, さんぷん, よんぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん. Half past is はん: くじはん = half past nine.
grammarPoints.watchFor: よじ・しちじ・くじ are the irregular hours — never よんじ, ななじ, きゅうじ.
grammarPoints.commonError: Saying よんじ for 4 o'clock. It is よじ.

grammarPoints.pattern: 〜ます ／ 〜ません ／ 〜ました ／ 〜ませんでした
grammarPoints.nameJa: おきます・おきません
grammarPoints.meaning: polite verbs across time and yes/no: do / don't / did / didn't
grammarPoints.explanation: Polite verbs end in ます, and you swap only the tail to move through time. Present: おきます = 'I get up / will get up'. Present negative: おきません = 'I don't / won't'. Past: おきました = 'I got up'. Past negative: おきませんでした = 'I didn't get up'. The stem (おき-) never changes. Mark the clock time with に — しちじに おきます = 'I get up at seven'.
grammarPoints.watchFor: に sits on a clock time (しちじに), but not on きょう, あした, or まいにち — those take no に.
grammarPoints.commonError: Adding に to まいにち or きょう. Say まいにち はたらきます, not まいにちに.

examples.ja: まいあさ ろくじに おきます。

examples.ja: きのう べんきょうしませんでした。
examples.reading: きのう べんきょうしませんでした。

examples.ja: どようびは はたらきません。
examples.reading: どようびは はたらきません。

grammarPoints.nameJa: くじから ごじまで
grammarPoints.meaning: from ... to / until — a span of time (and it works for places too)
grammarPoints.explanation: から marks the starting point ('from') and まで the end point ('until / to'). くじから ごじまで はたらきます = 'I work from nine to five'. You can use just one side: ろくじから = 'from six on'; はちじまで = 'until eight'. It stretches over days as well — げつようびから きんようびまで = 'from Monday to Friday'.
grammarPoints.watchFor: から on the start, まで on the end — くじから ごじまで, in that order.
grammarPoints.commonError: Swapping them: ごじから くじまで would mean 'from five to nine'. The start always takes から.

examples.ja: クラスは ろくじから はちじまでです。
examples.reading: クラスは ろくじから はちじまでです。
examples.en: Class is from six to eight.
examples.note: start + から, end + まで, then です.

examples.ja: げつようびから きんようびまで はたらきます。

examples.note: から／まで with days, not only clock times.

grammarPoints.pattern: きょうは 〜です ／ きのうは 〜でした（＋ ね）
grammarPoints.nameJa: きょうは かようびですね
grammarPoints.meaning: today is / yesterday was (a day is a noun) — plus ね, the gentle 'right?'
grammarPoints.explanation: For a noun like a day, です is 'is' and でした is 'was': きょうは かようびです = 'today is Tuesday'; きのうは げつようびでした = 'yesterday was Monday'. The negatives are じゃ ありません ('isn't') and じゃ ありませんでした ('wasn't'). Add ね at the end when you expect the other person to agree — like the English 'right?' or '..., isn't it': あしたは やすみですね = 'tomorrow's a day off, right?'
grammarPoints.watchFor: でした is the past of です (was) — a day is a noun, so you don't reach for a verb ending here.
grammarPoints.commonError: Saying きのうは げつようびです for 'yesterday was Monday'. Yesterday is past, so でした.
